I used Ryanair when I was a poor student because my ex-partner lived in Sweden and it was the cheapest way to get there. Honestly, the whole experience was awful. At the airport, staff confiscated my £20 bottle of L’Occitane shower gel, insisting it was over the liquid limit, even though it wasn’t. They told me I could get it back if I went to the airport pharmacy and bought a 100ml bottle. So I did exactly that, came back, and was told nobody had any idea what I was talking about. Brilliant. £20 gone, and I was absolutely furious.

They also charged me another £5 at the gate because I had a bottle of water in my hand luggage, despite the fact I’d bought it inside the airport.

Ryanair later stopped flying from Liverpool John Lennon Airport to Stockholm Skavsta, so I now fly Norwegian Air instead. Norwegian’s customer service is poor too, ironically, but at least the planes feel newer and less outdated than Ryanair’s.

You're not alone. The late August rain got to my Brandywine and Sungold. They're in raised beds and I'd been on a two day watering schedule. The plants were fine right up until that downpour. Now a bunch of the ripe and nearly ripe fruit is split. You're probably looking at the sudden water uptake as the cause. You can't really stop it once the fruit has set, but picking a little earlier next time would help. A thicker mulch layer might also keep the soil from swinging so hard. As for the ones that already went, cut the bad parts out and eat the rest. You aren't going to get sick from that.

The only thing that changes is the look of the thing. You'll find the same problem with pretty much any of the larger fruited varieties you have in the ground. They just can't keep up with the weather.
